No app code captures windows or renders offscreen. Confound: in (5) window 2 is also 43 % off screen, so less composited area could explain part of the drop; a run with a sliver of overlap, or both windows fully on an external display, would separate the two. Conclusion (likely, not proven without a minimal two-window control app): a window-server cost of two overlapping app windows, not the app's materials, level or glass. The harness now lays out windows that fit side by side without overlap (12e43d3; -WHPerfCascade YES restores the cascade); busy-10's three windows do not fit and still cascade, so the overlap cost is still measured there.
